angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,635,299 km at 45.28 pc = 0.48 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.0836 +/- 0.2117 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 45.28 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 2.351 (2.300 to 2.402) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 1,635,299 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.304 (2.263 to 2.345) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 9345 +/- 6.6 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6601750220152445440: teff_gspphot 9344.966 K (16th-84th percentiles 9338.602-9351.72), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6601750220152445440: teff_gspphot 9344.966 K (16th-84th percentiles 9338.602-9351.72), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/tiangang.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.058, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
